producer_original_scope_boundaries.purpose_cn: 记录候选所依赖的必要条件、量词/正则性/对象/极限/归一化、核心重计边界、作者未展开范围，以及影响使用的原文记号点。只定位，不改式，不判定作者数学对错。

group_objects.condition: Poincare group := discrete, torsion free, orientation preserving subgroup of Isom(H^d), d >= 2
Kleinian := Poincare group acting on H^3; Fuchsian := the H^2 case
quotient M_Gamma := H^d / Gamma is a hyperbolic manifold; pi is the universal Riemannian covering
the main theorem allows a general Kleinian group (not assumed finitely generated, not assumed geometrically finite) and assumes no finite Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure
degenerate Kleinian group := geometrically infinite finitely generated Kleinian group; used only in Corollary maincor, together with positive injectivity radius of M_Gamma

hypotheses_of_main_theorem.condition: there exist x,y in H^3 and alpha >= 0 with p_Gamma(x,y,t) >= t^(-alpha) for t large enough
hypotheses_of_main_theorem.note: one fixed pair; off-diagonal allowed; lower bound only for large t

hypotheses_of_main_theorem.condition: conclusion: for any x in H^3, N_Gamma(x,x,rho) is asymptotic to p_Gamma(x,x,rho/2) times V_3(rho) as rho tends to infinity
hypotheses_of_main_theorem.note: diagonal, all points, d = 3, heat time rho/2, ball-volume normalization

hypotheses_of_supporting_results.condition: propmaintheo: Poincare group, alpha > 0, x,y in H^d; f non zero in B^+_0(M_Gamma)
prop:operatorscomparison: same statement restated for H^3 with alpha > 0
propspectralprop: arbitrary dimension d; beta > 0; epsilon > 0; threshold beta log(rho)/rho
propheatkernellip: Kleinian group (dimension 3), alpha > 0, x,y in M_Gamma; local item on B(y,delta)
lemmapproxorbital: Poincare group, x,y in H^d, g decreasing, delta_epsilon depending only on epsilon, rho large
lemmaselbergstoformula: any lambda > 0 and rho > 0; s the root of s(d-1-s) = lambda with Re(s) at most (d-1)/2; c_(d-1) is the Euclidean unit-ball volume in R^(d-1)
lemmeheatdecreases: complete Riemannian manifold, function t -> p(x,x,t) for every x

regularity_and_object_conventions.condition: B^+_0(M) := measurable non-negative bounded compactly supported functions; continuity is NOT required
B^+_0(M) is contained in L^2(M); scalar product is the usual L^2 one with the Riemannian measure
Delta is taken positive on L^2(M), so the heat operator is exp(-t Delta) and the main theorem uses exp(-(rho/2) Delta)
heat kernel p_M of a complete manifold is the kernel of the unique L^2 solution of the Cauchy problem (quoted theorem)
p_Omega is the Dirichlet heat kernel of a bounded smooth domain (quoted theorem)
orbital function counts Gamma-orbit points in a closed ball of radius rho, i.e. distance <= rho; it descends to M_Gamma x M_Gamma x R_+
orbital operator O_Gamma^rho acts on B^+_0(M_Gamma) and is symmetric for the L^2 scalar product

quantifier_boundaries.heat_lower_bound_exists_one_pair_vs_all_: maintheo assumes the polynomial lower bound only for ONE pair (x,y) with x,y in H^3 (line 119), and concludes the asymptotic for ALL x on the diagonal (line 123). The upgrade from one off-diagonal pair to all points is exactly what propheatkernellip item 2 supplies (compact K, uniform C_K, all w,z in K, t > t_K). This quantifier shift is the heart of the candidate and must be preserved verbatim in any restatement.
quantifier_boundaries.diagonal_vs_offdiagonal: hypothesis is off-diagonal (x,y need not coincide); conclusion is on-diagonal (N_Gamma(x,x,rho), p_Gamma(x,x,rho/2)). The article explicitly contrasts this with the everywhere-valid weaker upper bound of artmoiheatcounting1 Th.1.2 (line 129).
quantifier_boundaries.t_vs_rho_over_2: the heat time in the conclusion is rho/2, not rho (lines 125, 241, 631, 709, 714). Any restatement using t = rho would change the statement.
quantifier_boundaries.large_time_and_large_radius: the hypothesis holds only for t large enough; the conclusion is a rho tends to infinity asymptotic. No uniformity in x is claimed beyond the asymptotic being pointwise for each fixed x.
quantifier_boundaries.spectral_quantifier_order: propspectralprop: for every beta > 0 there is C > 0 such that for every epsilon > 0 there is rho_0 > 0 such that for every rho > rho_0, items 1 and 2 hold. The constant C depends on beta only; rho_0 depends on beta and epsilon (lines 274-285).
quantifier_boundaries.local_version_delta: propheatkernellip item 1: for all epsilon > 0 there is delta > 0 such that there is t(x,y,alpha) > 0 with the two-sided comparison for all z in B(y,delta) and all t >= t(x,y,alpha). delta does not depend on t or z; t(x,y,alpha) may depend on x, y, alpha (lines 421-425).
quantifier_boundaries.compact_version: item 2: for every compact K there are C_K > 0 and t_K > 0 with p_Gamma(w,z,t) >= C_K t^(-alpha) for all w,z in K and all t > t_K (lines 427-430).
quantifier_boundaries.lemma_average_dimension: lemmaaverage is stated for a Poincare group in H^d with the normalization by V_d(rho), the hyperbolic ball volume (lines 217-226).
quantifier_boundaries.lemmapproxorbital_quantifiers: for all epsilon > 0 there is delta_epsilon > 0 such that for every 0 < delta <= delta_epsilon and rho large enough the two-sided comparison holds; g must be decreasing (lines 644-651).
quantifier_boundaries.selberg_transform_domain: nu_rho(lambda) is defined for rho > 0 and all lambda > 0 via s(d-1-s) = lambda with Re(s) at most (d-1)/2; for lambda above ((d-1)/2)^2 the real part is constant equal to (d-1)/2 (lines 259-262, 880-884, 992-996).

normalization_points.point: V_d(rho) is the volume of a hyperbolic ball of radius rho in H^d; V_d(rho) is asymptotic to V_d exp((d-1)rho) and V_3 denotes the constant in that asymptotic (lines 115, 640, 650)
N_Gamma is divided by V_d(rho) to obtain the kernel of the orbital operator (lines 221-226)
nu_rho(lambda) is defined as the mean over B(o,rho) of y^s with o = (0,...,0,1) in the upper half-space model and measure dx_1...dx_(d-1)dy / y^d (lines 259-262, 898-901, 1129-1131)
c_(d-1) is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball in R^(d-1) (line 901)
theta(rho,r) is defined for rho > |r| by (2(cosh rho - cosh r) / e^rho)^((d-1)/2), bounded by 2^((d-1)/2) (lines 888-892)

shared_scope: Kleinian means discrete torsion-free orientation-preserving subgroup of Isom(H3); do not add finite-volume, finite BMS measure, finite generation or positive injectivity radius to the main theorem.

Main hypothesis: there EXIST one fixed x,y and alpha>=0 with p_Gamma(x,y,t)>=t^(-alpha) for sufficiently large t. Conclusion: for EACH fixed x the diagonal asymptotic N_Gamma(x,x,rho)~p_Gamma(x,x,rho/2)*V_3(rho). Do not demand an all-point-pair hypothesis or claim uniformity over all x.
V_3(rho) is the full hyperbolic ball volume as authored. Keep heat time rho/2, positive Laplacian and exp(-time*Delta); do not replace the normalization by a new closed-form constant.

Only Proposition3.9 supplies uniform C_K,t_K over w,z in a fixed compact K. Its local delta is uniform in the near point and independent of time; retain the author's stated dependencies and sufficiently-large-time order.
Main alpha>=0 versus support propositions alpha>0 remains literal, including proof749 alpha>=0; no assistant endpoint argument.

Operators comparison2.3 at233-243 literally states Hd with rho/2;4.1 at624-633 states H3. The proof uses3D-only3.9 at759-766 and beta/2 at824-826. General-d spectral2.6/4.4 has rho/(d-1). Preserve this scope variant without certifying a general-dimensional operator comparison.

B0plus consists of measurable nonnegative bounded compactly supported functions, not assumed continuous; comparison requires nonzero f. No measure/smoothness/pointwise strengthening is inserted.
